title: Tesla cuts AI5 chip memory to 96GB to secure Optimus production supply
key_facts: Elon Musk said on X that Tesla cut the memory on its next-generation chips: AI5 in half to 72GB of LPDDR5 and AI6 by a third to 144GB of LPDDR6.
Musk called it 'the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production' and said it also greatly reduces cost.
He expects 'a negligible effect on Optimus performance' because memory bandwidth, which is unchanged, limits these systems more than total capacity.
He later raised AI5 to 96GB because 'Tesla would otherwise be the only company using the min RAM version of LP5'; AI5 ends up a third below its original plan, like AI6.
Micron has estimated each humanoid robot could need about 200GB of RAM; memory supply is tight across the industry.
Samsung recently began trial production of AI5 at its Taylor, Texas fab, with mass production aimed at 2027; AI5 is not coming to cars first.
Not a Tesla App is dated 3 Oct 2026 and says Musk posted 'earlier this week'; a Wccftech headline dated 1 Oct 2026 carries the 72GB cut.
quote_evidence: He called it “the only way to get enough volume for Optimus production,” and said the move also greatly reduces cost.
As for performance, Musk said Tesla expects “a negligible effect on Optimus performance.”

why_it_matters_hint: Memory shortages are limiting how many humanoid robots Tesla can build, and the 'no performance loss' claim is Musk's own.
event_date: Musk's X posts about 1-2 Oct 2026 (Wccftech headlines dated 1 and 2 Oct; Not a Tesla App 3 Oct)
